key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over months to years. LOCATION: GENERALIZED symptoms. DURATION: Chronic progressive condition. CHARACTER: CHOREA, cognitive decline, behavioral changes. AGGRAVATING: STRESS, fatigue, medication changes. RELIEVING: SUPPORTIVE care, medications. TIMING: Chronic progressive, symptoms worsen over time. SEVERITY: 3-7/10, mild to moderate. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: CHOREA, cognitive decline, behavioral changes, may have psychiatric symptoms. KEY POSITIVES: Chorea, cognitive decline, behavioral changes, family history. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Severe neurological deficits with altered mental status - possible severe Huntington's flare, call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
Signs of respiratory failure - difficulty breathing, cyanosis, altered mental status - call 911
